summary:
FMLink reports August US labor market data with a focus on facility management hiring in local government and education. Local government and education added 42,000 jobs in August, largely offsetting a decline the previous month. The category includes public universities, colleges, and related administrative roles, and was among the top contributors to total job gains. Other gains came from food services and drinking places (59,000) and leisure/hospitality (62,000).

Overall, employers created 162,000 jobs in August, far surpassing forecaster expectations. July figures were revised upward by 21,000 to a gain of 51,000, reversing the Bureau of Labor Statistics' earlier report that employers cut 23,000 jobs in July. June payroll gains were also revised higher, indicating the summer job market was stronger than economists predicted. ADP's National Employment Report, released September 2, showed a much lower figure of 38,000 private-sector jobs added in August. The unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, and the labor force participation rate rose to 61.6% after falling to 61.4% the prior month. The article frames the data as encouraging after spring uncertainty about hiring momentum, saying the labor market appears to be on sturdier footing.

The bulk of the piece is a listing of open facility management roles from the FMLink Career Center. Higher education postings include Associate Vice Chancellor and Chief Facilities Officer at Vanderbilt, Executive Director of Facilities at Harvard Medical School, Associate Director of Facilities at University of Georgia, Associate VP for Facilities Management and Campus Planner at University at Albany (SUNY), Director of College Facilities Planning at University of Delaware, Director of Facilities Planning and Construction at Santa Monica College, and a Mechanical Maintenance Person at Roger Williams University. Government postings include roles at Systems Application & Technologies (US Army Dugway Proving Ground), NY CREATES, Leidos, Trademasters Services, and Anser. The piece promotes the FMLink Job Board and its career planning resources.
